purpose: Document oracle failure scenarios, their impact on settlement, and recovery procedures

failureModes.name: Single Oracle Offline (Outage)
failureModes.scenario: One of 5 oracles stops responding; others report normally
requirements: Monitor oracle response latency (alert if > 10 seconds)
Mark oracle offline after 5 consecutive timeouts

failureModes.name: Two Oracles Offline (Cascade Outage)
failureModes.scenario: Two of 5 oracles down (e.g., shared infrastructure failure)
failureModes.userImpact: Settlement blocked; requires manual operator override or timeout recovery
recoveryProcedure: wait 5 minutes for oracles to recover
if still offline after 5 min, trigger 30-minute timeout
if consensus not restored after 30 min, escalate to manual override
manual override: 2-of-3 operators + 6-hour timelock can force settlement at last-known-good price
preventionMeasures: use geographically distributed oracle providers (different cloud regions)
use different data sources (Coinbase, Kraken, Binance - not shared infrastructure)
monitor oracle provider status pages
implement redundant data fetching (fallback to backup provider)

failureModes.name: Oracle Price Disagreement (≥1% divergence)
failureModes.scenario: Oracles report conflicting prices; 2 say $1.00, 3 say $0.99
failureModes.cause: Stale feed, CEX data desync, network latency, market flash move
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: if divergence > 2%, supermajority consensus fails (conflicting outcomes)
failureModes.userImpact: Settlement blocked; affected users cannot execute trades until consensus restored
failureModes.exampleImpact: Liquidation oracle disagrees; borrower stays underwater or gets unfairly liquidated
recoveryProcedure: covenant detects disagreement (more than 2 oracles outside consensus band)
automatically publish 'price-divergence' event to attestation registry
pause new settlements for 1 minute (allow staleness check to resolve)
after 1 minute, if agreement restored, resume settlement
if still diverged after 1 minute, require manual operator review
preventionMeasures: implement consensus band checks (reject > 2% deviation from median)
fetch prices from multiple sources within same 500ms window
add price stability checks: reject 10x move in 1 minute
monitor oracle-source latency (alert if > 2 seconds apart)
implement rolling medians (use last 3 prices to smooth noise)

failureModes.name: Stale Oracle Feed (No Update)
failureModes.scenario: Oracle reports last price from 10 minutes ago (should refresh every 5 min)
failureModes.cause: Oracle service crashed, network connectivity lost, operator forgot to restart
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: if 3+ oracles stale, consensus uses outdated data (settlement may be wrong)
failureModes.userImpact: Settlement uses stale prices; liquidations may use wrong collateral value
failureModes.exampleImpact: Collateral worth $100 but oracle reports $120; liquidator profits on price decay
preventionMeasures: set 5-minute staleness limit per oracle
reject prices older than staleness limit
if consensus has > 2 stale oracles, block settlement
implement automatic fallback: use 'last-known-good' price with exponential decay penalty
monitor staleness actively; alert operator if any oracle hasn't updated in 3 minutes
recoveryProcedure: operator is alerted of stale oracle
operator investigates oracle service status
restart oracle service if crashed
if stale > 30 min, enable manual override (2-of-3 operators can force price)

failureModes.name: Oracle Operator Key Compromised
failureModes.scenario: Attacker obtains oracle operator's signing key; can forge any price
failureModes.cause: key phishing, server breach, insider threat
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: attacker can sign arbitrary prices; 4-of-5 supermajority requires 4 keys, so attacker needs 4 keys for full control
failureModes.userImpact: Attacker can trigger false liquidations, steal collateral, or crash market
failureModes.maxDamageScenario: attacker controls 4 of 5 oracle keys; can force settlement at any price for 1 block
preventionMeasures: rotate oracle keys quarterly
use hardware wallets for oracle signing keys
enforce multi-sig on key management (2-of-3 operators approve key rotation)
monitor key usage patterns (alert if unusual signing frequency)
implement rate limits (reject > 10 price updates per minute per oracle)
emergencyProcedure: remove oracle from active set (reduce to 4 oracles)
mark all prices signed by compromised key as 'untrusted'
trigger manual price validation for all recent settlements (last 24 hours)
escalate to governance for oracle replacement

failureModes.name: Malicious Oracle Collusion (3-of-5 Agree on False Price)
failureModes.scenario: Three oracle operators collude to report false prices; trigger false liquidations
failureModes.cause: operator bribery, shared incentive misalignment, hostile takeover
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: 3-of-5 supermajority requires 4 oracles; collusion of 3 is insufficient
failureModes.userImpact: Mitigated by supermajority; even if 3 collude, 4th oracle prevents bad consensus
failureModes.maxDamageScenario: if attacker controls 4+ oracles, can force any settlement; requires either compromise of 4 keys or collusion of 4 operators
preventionMeasures: diversify oracle operators (different companies, different incentives)
use reputable established oracle providers (Chainlink, Uniswap, dYdX)
implement oracle reputation scoring (track historical accuracy)
enforce supermajority consensus (4-of-5 makes collusion harder)
monitor price deviation (alert if multiple oracles suddenly diverge)
governance_escalation: if 2+ oracles show correlated price errors over time, governance may vote to replace them
implement emergency pause (2-of-3 multisig operators can pause settlement for 24 hours)
escalate to community vote for oracle replacement

failureModes.name: Consensus Timeout (No Resolution)
failureModes.scenario: Oracles in deadlock; < 4 agree on outcome; settlement cannot proceed
failureModes.cause: network partition, oracle disagreement, 2+ oracles offline simultaneously
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: cannot reach 4-of-5 supermajority; settlement blocked indefinitely
failureModes.userImpact: Users stuck in pending settlement state; collateral locked; opportunity cost
failureModes.recoveryTime: operator manual override (30-60 minutes) or automatic timeout fallback (1-6 hours)
recoveryProcedure: 1. Automatic phase (0-30 minutes): system waits for consensus to resolve
2. Operator alert phase (30-60 minutes): operators notified, investigate cause
3. Manual override phase (60+ minutes): 2-of-3 operators vote to use 'last-known-good' price with timestamp
4. Governance escalation (> 6 hours): if still unresolved, escalate to community vote
preventionMeasures: pre-commit oracle prices (require price commitment before use)
use quorum-based consensus (simple majority 3-of-5 for faster settlement, supermajority 4-of-5 for high-value)
implement timelock mechanism (force settlement at last-known-good price after 1 hour)
diversify oracle data sources (reduce single-point-of-failure in data fetch)

failureModes.name: Flash Price Move (Legitimate Market Move > 5%)
failureModes.scenario: Market suddenly moves 5-10% (e.g., Fed announcement); oracles report conflicting prices
failureModes.cause: Legitimate market volatility; oracles fetch at different times, see different prices
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: oracles show > 2% deviation; supermajority consensus fails
failureModes.userImpact: Settlement delayed by 1-5 minutes (oracles realign on actual price)
preventionMeasures: use price stability checks (allow max 2% divergence for 10-minute moving average)
implement consensus band (median ±2% for normal assets, ±0.01% for stable-value)
use time-weighted averages (smooth out flash moves)
require price update frequency (e.g., at least every 5 seconds during high volatility)
failureModes.operatorNotes: This is expected behavior during volatile markets. Settlement automatically resumes once oracles realign. No manual intervention needed.

failureModes.name: No Oracle Confidence (All Oracles Report Error)
failureModes.scenario: All 5 oracles unable to fetch price (e.g., all CEXes offline, network partition)
failureModes.cause: global internet outage, CEX DDoS attack, oracle service cascade failure
failureModes.impactOnConsensus: impossible to reach any consensus; settlement completely blocked
failureModes.userImpact: All settlements blocked; users cannot move collateral; liquidations paused
failureModes.recoveryTime: wait for infrastructure recovery (hours to days) or governance override
recoveryProcedure: 1. Automatic phase: system broadcasts 'zero-confidence' alert to all users
2. Operator phase (after 1 hour): operators vote to use historical average price with 5% haircut
3. Governance phase (after 6 hours): if still no consensus, escalate to community vote for recovery mechanism
preventionMeasures: use backup oracle providers (not correlated with primary 5)
implement historical price fallback (use last-known-good price for up to 24 hours with penalty)
use on-chain price feeds (if available) as fallback
implement manual operator override with timelock

tier1_must_have: Alert operators if any oracle offline
Implement automatic fallback to last-known-good price after 30-minute timeout
tier2_should_have: Implement price stability checks (reject > 2% move in 1 minute)
Build operator dashboard with oracle health metrics
tier3_nice_to_have: Implement reputation scoring for oracle accuracy
Use hardware wallets for oracle signing keys
Implement Byzantine fault tolerance (support weighted oracle consensus)
Build governance escalation UI for community override votes

notes: This failure-modes document assumes 5 oracles with 4-of-5 supermajority consensus. Adjust recovery times and thresholds if using different oracle count or consensus model. For stable-value assets, use stricter deviation bands (0.01% instead of 2%).
